transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Laura (Product), Alex (Eng), Priya (PM), Samir (SRE), Diego (Infra), Maya (QA)

Summary:
Brief triage working session to finalize C2 launch fallbacks, confirm SLOs/SLA gating, and assign owners for runbook + perf validation. Focus on quick mitigation paths (canary rollbacks, model quant variants, routing policies), and a short list of critical tests to run pre-release.

Topics covered:
- Priority fallback flavors: canary roll, regional failover, model-variant fallback (quantized/trimmed attention), traffic shaping
- SLO gating thresholds and emergency throttles
- Kernel and runtime fallback behaviors under KV cache pressure
- Release checklist gaps and required smoke tests
- Incident lessons from last weekend's perf spike

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Laura: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. I think we have, uh, 70 minutes-ish. Goal is to lock down what we need to do so C2 can go green next week. I'll kick off with the current open risks.
[00:00:15] Priya: Quick add — stakeholders in SaaS and Platform want the canary to be able to fail to a cheaper variant rather than fully fall back to the old model. So routing -> degen path is important.
[00:00:30] Alex: Yep. A degen path when used carefully cuts cost but we saw last time the quality drop was more visible on short prompts. We should define exact trigger thresholds — like token latency over 300ms P95 for 3 minutes, or error rate > 1%.
[00:00:45] Samir: And also make sure the throttle S-L-O isn't too aggressive, we don't want cascading queuing. Last weekend our throttle kicked in and the backlog spiked on the ingress.
[00:00:58] Diego: Right, the backlog was because the KV cache thrash created big mem pressure. The runtime then switched to fallback kernels and that increased per-token time. The transcription from the earlier note said "kayv cache" which was amusing — it is KV cache.
[00:01:15] Maya: For tests I want a matrix: short convo, long seq 32k, embeddings rerank path. Especially the 32k sequence with warm KV and cold KV scenarios.
[00:01:30] Alex: On kernel fallback — I did a spike: when we hit the degenerate attention path the latency tripled in the worst case, but with 8-bit quant it still stayed under 2.5x. We need to quantify that across GPUs.
[00:01:45] Priya: Can we get concrete numbers by next Monday? The release board wants a small table: baseline P95, fallback P95, cost delta per 1k tokens.
[00:01:58] Alex: I can run across A100 and H100 but availability's limited. Diego, can you confirm a small dedicated slot to run microbenchmarks?
[00:02:10] Diego: I can carve out 2 nodes in our dedicated pool for a day, but we should optimize the tests; don't run full shards. Also note region mapping — if we route to eu-west as fallback, NVidia vs AWS instance perf diff is important.
[00:02:25] Samir: On SRE side, we need an auto-failover step: if region degraded, route traffic to secondary with 10% canary, evaluate for 10 minutes, then ramp. If that fails, fall back to quantized variant locally. I'd like this codified in the runbook.
[00:02:40] Laura: Agreed. So runbook must show the order: canary region -> degraded region -> local quant variant -> full rollback. Also include communication steps.
[00:02:52] Maya: About smoke tests — we should have quick post-deploy checks: latency P95 < X ms, top-10 prompt quality eval doesn't regress > Y% (automated sampling), and error rate < 0.5%.
[00:03:10] Priya: On quality checks, we should have a small set of prompts that are weighted for conversation and code generation for internal customers. We'll need someone to pick the prompts.
[00:03:25] Alex: I'll bring a baseline prompt set; Maya can add anti-regression ones. We should keep them under 200 prompts to keep evals fast.
[00:03:40] Samir: One more operational note — alerting. Last incident we didn't have a good signal for the kernel fallback rate. We should emit a metric for "kernel_fallback_count" and an SLI around fallback_rate > 0.5% at P95.
[00:04:00] Diego: Implementation detail — runtime already emits kernel hints, but the mapping from hint to fallback_count is lossy. I'll add a field in the trace to be explicit so Firehose can alert.
[00:04:15] Laura: Great. Let's run through the edge-case scenarios: what do we do if quant variant introduces hallucination patterns or hallucination rate increases?
[00:04:28] Alex: If hallucination goes up, fallback to a shorter context window and enable deterministic sampling for that burst. It's ugly but buys time. We need a plan to detect hallucination automatically — maybe measuring semantic drift against gold outputs is heavy.
[00:04:45] Maya: We can instrument with a cheap classifier for hallucination on certain tasks, but not general. For release, threshold-based manual check may be acceptable.
[00:05:00] Priya: Legal and compliance flagged data residency for VPC customers; if we route to a fallback region we must ensure data doesn't leave the EU for EU customers. That gating is critical.
[00:05:12] Diego: We have region-based routing knobs. For enterprise customers with residency constraints we must never route out of-region — the runbook should clearly exclude those accounts from automated regional fallback.
[00:05:25] Samir: Also include a kill switch that can isolate the dedicated pool per-customer if needed.
[00:05:33] Alex: Returning to perf numbers: I'll prioritize a table of baseline vs quant vs kernel-fallback on the matrices: short convo (32 tokens), medium (512), long (8k, 32k). That will help product decide acceptable SLO gates.
[00:05:50] Laura: Who is owner for the runbook?
[00:05:54] Alex: I can own the testing portion, but Laura should own the runbook doc and comms.
[00:06:00] Laura: I'll own the doc and coordinate with Priya for stakeholder comms.
[00:06:05] Priya: For release gating — we want a preflight that includes perf table, smoke tests pass, SRE checklist complete, stakeholder sign-off. If any item is red, we delay.
[00:06:18] Maya: On smoke tests automation — I can write the harness to run as a post-rollout job and fail loudly if thresholds aren't met.
[00:06:28] Samir: We should rehearse a simulated region outage tomorrow in staging to validate routing and auto-failover. Can we time-box it to 30 minutes?
[00:06:36] Diego: Yes, I can schedule the rehearsal — note it will impact other staging tests.
[00:06:42] Laura: Good. Add rehearsal to the calendar and invite Platform and Support.
[00:06:50] Priya: Ok, quick incident learnings from weekend: the perf spike was traced to a combination of a bad prompt pattern causing repeated long decode loops and a suboptimal caching header TTL. We should add a TTL tuning test.
[00:07:05] Alex: I think the decode loop bug is partially fixed but still shows in certain multi-hop prompts. I'll pull a log sample and attach it to the runbook.
[00:07:18] Maya: For the TTL, smaller TTLs helped reduce stale prefix hits but increased KV load. We need to pick a sensible default and make it configurable per-tenant.
[00:07:30] Samir: Actionable: Priya to list top-5 tenants with residency needs and stake them out from automated routing.
[00:07:38] Priya: Will do.
[00:07:40] Laura: Anything else?
[00:07:42] Diego: Minor but important — verify H100 kernel fallback behaves same as A100; last time the logs showed a different stack trace which confused the oncall.
[00:07:52] Alex: I'll add explicit test for both.
[00:07:55] Maya: One more on QA — we should include a manual tasting session for high-risk prompts after canary ramp. Two engineers should sanity-check.
[00:08:05] Laura: Ok that's in.
[00:08:07] Priya: Recap and owners?
[00:08:10] Laura: Recap: Laura owns runbook + comms; Alex owns perf numbers and quant prototype; Samir owns SLO knobs and rehearsal; Diego owns kernel-fallback instrumentation and cluster scheduling verification; Maya owns smoke harness and post-rollout tests; Priya owns stakeholder list and residency gating. Dates noted in action items.
[00:08:30] Alex: I'll post the perf artifact to the team drive and start the runs tonight.
[00:08:36] Samir: I'll schedule the simulated region outage for 2026-07-09 09:00 PT and invite folks.
[00:08:44] Maya: I'll ship the smoke harness by 2026-07-13.
[00:08:48] Laura: Great. Meeting adjourned — thanks all.

Post-meeting notes (auto):
- Attachments referenced: perf-spike-logs.zip (alex), canary-routing-diagram.png (diego), preflight-checklist-v2.md (laura).
- Follow-up rehearsal scheduled: 2026-07-09 09:00 PT (Samir/Diego).
- Risk highlight: KV cache thrash -> kernel fallback -> P95 latency spike. Need concrete perf delta across instance types before go/no-go.

End of transcript.
